kill_fact:
The catalyst has fired and nothing dated, binding or agency-controlled replaces it. Verified against the company's own 26 June 2026 release: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) 'for the treatment of thyroid eye disease regardless of thyroid eye disease activity or duration', four days ahead of the 30 June 2026 PDUFA target action date, with no advisory committee, no complete response letter, and immediate launch -- physicians 'can prescribe Lumvoa tomorrow'. That is the best available version of the event this sleeve underwrote, and the tape refused it: the live quote is $19.70, against a 50-day average of $17.66 and a 200-day average of $24.03, inside a 52-week range of $13.18 to $34.29. The stock popped roughly 12% on 29 June and gave it all back inside a month.

What remains on the calendar is not a forcing function. The second-quarter report around 5 August 2026 covers roughly one month of selling and can neither settle nor break the question. Management's 'six to nine months to broad coverage' is a company expectation, not a scheduled event. The elegrobart BLA targeted for the first quarter of 2027 is a submission Viridian controls, not a regulator's deadline. The European decision has no published date. There is no merger agreement, no deal price, no CVR, no financing contingency and no contractual backstop anywhere in this position. A special-situations sleeve exists to own a dated event with a bounded loss; what is left here is an ordinary first-product commercial launch against a six-year incumbent, and it should be underwritten as one or not at all.

The file reaches the right conclusion -- verdict C, conviction 2, catalyst_status FIRED, 'this belongs off the book' -- so the kill is not a disagreement about the call. It is a confirmation of the call plus two filing-level errors that both cut the same way: the downside is thinner than written. The bull file's cash bridge omits a $55.1 million cash outflow that the 8-K discloses, and understates the convertible principal by $25.0 million. Corrected, net cash is about $736 million and the estimated floor is about $8.00, not $8.50 -- which widens the stated 57% downside rather than narrowing it. The asymmetry does not survive on either leg.
corrections:
1) MISSING CASH OUTFLOW -- material, load-bearing, omitted entirely. The file's bridge runs '$762.2m at 31 March + $334.7m net May proceeds + $75m DRI milestone - burn'. It never accounts for the Hercules Capital payoff. Viridian's 8-K (event date 27 May 2026, filed 28 May 2026) discloses that the company paid approximately $55.1 million covering 'all outstanding principal, accrued and unpaid interest, fees, costs and expenses' under the 1 April 2022 Loan and Security Agreement, and that the agreement was terminated. This was the stated use of proceeds in the 6 May pricing release. $55.1 million of cash left the building and the file's bridge does not show it.

2) CONVERTIBLE PRINCIPAL UNDERSTATED -- material. The file uses '$225 million of 2032 convertible notes' throughout, including in every net-cash and floor calculation. $225.0 million was the PRICING figure of 6 May 2026. The closing 8-K (event 6 May 2026, filed 11 May 2026) records that the offering completed at $250,000,000 aggregate principal of 1.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032, 'including the exercise in full of the underwriters' option to purchase up to an additional $25.0 million'. Net proceeds were approximately $242.0 million on the notes and approximately $117.0 million on the 7,352,942 common shares at $17.00 -- roughly $359.0 million of aggregate net proceeds, not the $334.7 million the file carries. Debt is $250.0 million, not $225.0 million.

3) NET RESULT, and it runs against the bull. Corrected bridge: $762.2m + $359.0m net proceeds - $55.1m Hercules payoff + $75.0m DRI milestone = $1,141.1m, less a launch-weighted second quarter (~$115m) and roughly a further month (~$40m), gives cash of approximately $986 million. So the file's headline 'roughly $1.0 billion of cash' SURVIVES -- the extra $24.3m of net proceeds largely offsets the missed $55.1m payoff. But NET cash is $986m - $250m = approximately $736 million, not the $790 million claimed: overstated by about $54 million. Per share that is roughly $6.70 on ~109.8 million common (file: $7.20) and roughly $5.93 on an as-converted ~124 million (file: $6.30). Carrying the file's own $2.00 to $2.50 strategic residual, the estimated floor is approximately $8.00, not $8.50 -- so downside from $19.70 is about 59%, not 57%.

4) MINOR -- note conversion shares. At $250.0 million principal and a $24.65 conversion price the notes represent about 10.1 million shares, not the 9.1 million stated. The file's fully diluted total of 'near 134 million' happens to land correctly (124.1m as-converted + 10.1m = ~134.2m) despite being built from a wrong component.

5) CONFIRMED AS WRITTEN, no change needed. Every other load-bearing fact checked out against primary sources: approval 26 June 2026 versus a 30 June 2026 PDUFA date; the 'regardless of activity or duration' label; five intravenous infusions every three weeks over about twelve weeks; REVEAL-1 topline of 30 March 2026 showing 54% (Q4W) and 63% (Q8W) proptosis response against an 18% placebo rate at week 24, with 51% complete diplopia resolution versus 16% placebo; the DRI Healthcare royalty financing of up to $300 million with tiered royalties of 7.5% on U.S. net sales of veligrotug and VRDN-003 and a $75 million milestone triggered by the approval; cash of $762.2 million at 31 March 2026; a first-quarter net loss of $104.9 million on $141 thousand of revenue with R&D of $77.6 million and SG&A of $38.7 million; 116,757,742 as-converted shares at 31 March 2026 (102.5 million common plus ~14.3 million preferred equivalents), supporting both the ~110 million common and ~125 million as-converted counts; and the $19.70 price with 50-day $17.66, 200-day $24.03 and a $13.18 to $34.29 52-week range. The elegrobart BLA remains guided to the first quarter of 2027. No hidden disqualifier was found beyond the fired catalyst itself: no boxed warning (hearing impairment, hyperglycemia at ~12%, infusion reactions at ~9% and IBD are warnings and precautions, and are class effects shared with the incumbent), and no going-concern or financing contingency.
evidence: Viridian Therapeutics press release, 26 June 2026, 'Viridian Therapeutics Announces U.S. FDA Approval and Launch of Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) for the Treatment of Thyroid Eye Disease' (Form 8-K Ex-99.1, CIK 0001590750, accession 0001193125-26-286273): 'Lumvoa is indicated for the treatment of thyroid eye disease regardless of thyroid eye disease activity or duration'; dosing is 'five intravenous infusions, each given every three weeks' over 12 weeks; launch immediate, 'physicians can prescribe Lumvoa tomorrow'. The PDUFA target action date was 30 June 2026, so the event fired four days early and favourably. https://investors.viridiantherapeutics.com/news/news-details/2026/Viridian-Therapeutics-Announces-U-S--FDA-Approval-and-Launch-of-Lumvoa-veligrotug-vvze-for-the-Treatment-of-Thyroid-Eye-Disease/default.aspx -- CATALYST IS SPENT; no dated, binding, agency-controlled event remains.

Viridian Therapeutics Form 8-K, event date 6 May 2026, filed 11 May 2026 (CIK 0001590750, accession 0001193125-26-216709): the company completed a $250,000,000 aggregate principal offering of 1.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032, 'including the exercise in full of the underwriters' option to purchase up to an additional $25.0 million aggregate principal amount of the Notes, solely to cover over-allotments', with net proceeds of approximately $242.0 million; and 7,352,942 common shares at $17.00 with net proceeds of approximately $117.0 million; conversion rate 40.5680 shares per $1,000 (~$24.65), maturity 15 May 2032; stated use of proceeds includes repaying 'all outstanding indebtedness under the Loan and Security Agreement, dated April 1, 2022, with Hercules Capital, Inc.' https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590750/000119312526216709/d154062d8k.htm -- CORRECTS the file's $225 million notes figure and its $334.7 million net-proceeds figure.

Viridian Therapeutics Form 8-K, event date 27 May 2026, filed 28 May 2026: Viridian paid approximately $55.1 million representing 'all outstanding principal, accrued and unpaid interest, fees, costs and expenses' under the 1 April 2022 Hercules Capital Loan and Security Agreement, whereupon 'all obligations, covenants, debts and liabilities of the Company under the Loan Agreement were satisfied and discharged in full, and the Loan Agreement ... terminated'. https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/VRDN/8-k-viridian-therapeutics-inc-de-reports-material-event-e657deaf3dc8.html -- a $55.1 million cash outflow the bull file's cash bridge omits entirely; net cash is ~$736 million, not ~$790 million, and the floor is ~$8.00, not $8.50.

Viridian Therapeutics first-quarter 2026 results, released 5 May 2026: cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $762.2 million at 31 March 2026; net loss of $104.9 million (versus $86.9 million in the prior-year quarter); R&D of $77.6 million; SG&A of $38.7 million; total revenue of $141 thousand; and '116,757,742 shares of common stock outstanding on an as-converted basis' at 31 March 2026. Separately, DRI Healthcare confirmed a $75 million milestone payable on the Lumvoa approval under the October 2025 royalty financing of up to $300 million, which carries tiered royalties of 7.5% of annual U.S. net sales of veligrotug and VRDN-003. https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/viridian-therapeutics-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-highlights-recent-progress -- CONFIRMS the burn, the share-count base and the permanent royalty drag as written.
